title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.

title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.

title: Introduction to Neuroscience Clinical Trials
description: Provides an overview of the science of clinical development of treatments for neurological disease and injury.

title: Ecosystem Ecology
description: A mechanistic perspective on ecosystem processes. Covers ecosystem development, element cycling, and interactions with plants and microbes. The role of ecosystems in environmental change is also addressed.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI E106 or EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 60A or CHEM 51C

title: Experimental Microbiology Laboratory
description: Introductory general microbiology designed for preprofessional biology majors. Includes microscopy, cultivation of bacteria, morphological and biochemical characterization of bacteria, microbial metabolism, growth and genetics, microorganisms and human disease, and interactions of microorganisms with the environment. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 99 and ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 )

title: Selfish DNA
description: Focuses on the genetics and evolution of selfish DNA, and introduces necessary background knowledge from molecular biology, cytogenetics, and bioinformatics.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H94 or BIO SCI H97

title: Advanced Topics in Immunology
description: Literature-based, interactive discussions focused on review of seminal historic and recent immunology literature. Student responsibilities include reading, critical evaluation, and discussion of manuscripts.

title: History of Neuroscience
description: An overview of the conceptual and technical foundations of contemporary neuroscience from ancient times to the present. The subjects include synapses, neurons, brain organization, sensory, motor and regulatory systems, learning and memory, human brain function and dysfunction.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or PSCI 115D or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B and COGS 9C)

title: Bioimaging and Spatial Biotechnology
description: Covers the theory, history, and application of light microscopy, electron microscopy, and spatial biotechniques in a non-mathematical way. Starts with principles of various microscopes, and discusses recent innovations in imaging techniques such as super-resolution microscopy.

title: Marine Biology
description: Examines the biotic and abiotic factors influencing the physiology, distribution, abundances, interactions, and evolution of marine organisms and the roles of those organisms in mediating ecosystem services and functions. A field trip is required. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

title: Human Biology I
description: Provides an in-depth look at cutting-edge topics in physiology and epidemiology as they relate to global issues of ethics, anthropology, and socioeconomics, providing the student with an understanding of human health beyond basic biological function.

title: Human Biology II
description: Provides an in-depth look at cutting-edge topics in physiology and epidemiology as they relate to global issues of ethics, anthropology, and socioeconomics, providing the student with an understanding of human health beyond basic biological function.

title: Human Biology III
description: Provides an in-depth look at cutting-edge topics in physiology and epidemiology as they relate to global issues of ethics, anthropology, and socioeconomics, providing the student with an understanding of human health beyond basic biological function.

title: Immunology with Hematology
description: Antibodies, antigens, antigen-antibody reactions, cells and tissues of lymphoreticular and hematopoietic systems, and individual and collective components of cell-mediated and humoral immune response.

title: Advanced Immunology Laboratory
description: Emphasis is placed on learning modern techniques in immunology such as ELISAs, western blotting, and immunofluorescent staining assays. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and BIO SCI M121

title: Drug Addiction
description: Provides a comprehensive overview of topics in the addiction field, including drug pharmacology, models/approaches to investigate addiction, brain circuits, genetics, epigenetics, and the cellular and molecular biology of drug addiction.

title: General Microbiology
description: Comparative metabolism of small molecules and cell structure and relationship to microbial classification. Macromolecule synthesis and regulation, sporulation, cell division, growth, and effect of antibiotics.

title: Scientific Argumentation and Critical Thinking
description: Explicitly teaches argument structure, deductive logic, inductive logic, and common fallacies in the biology context. Students identify assumptions and fallacies in faulty arguments and data figures and learn to compose sound arguments.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 93 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Introduction to Computational Biology
description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2D or MATH 3A or STATS 7 or STATS 8

title: Human Neuroimaging Lab
description: Hands-on laboratory course in human neuroimaging, with particular emphasis on using MRI to understand brain function and how it changes over the course of the lifespan and with disease.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 93 and ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 )

title: Biology of Integrative Medecine
description: Presentation of biological principles and the latest clinical and basic research on complementary and alternative therapies (e.g., mind-body medicine, energy medicine, herbal medicine, acupuncture, manipulative therapies) and their integration with Western medicine. Lectures supplemented by demonstrations and hands-on learning sessions.

title: Virology
description: Replication of viruses in populations, animals, and the host cell. The effects of viral infection on populations, individuals, and specific molecular effects on the target cell. Role of viral infections in cancer and degenerative diseases.

title: Viral Pathogenesis and Immunity
description: The mechanisms of viral pathogenesis and of host resistance to viruses are explored in detail. HIV-1 and Influenza-A are used as examples. In each case, viral replication, cytopathic effects, immune response, and viral evasion are discussed.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M124A . Recommended: BIO SCI M122

title: Model Systems in Biology
description: On the use of animal and in vitro models in biomedical research, focusing on assumptions, promises, limitations, and compromises.

title: Molecular Biology of Cancer
description: Covers topics in basic molecular and cellular cancer biology with focus on oncogenes and tumor suppressors, cancer signaling pathways, mechanisms of cancer initiation and progression, metastasis, tumor microenvironment, and modern cancer therapeutics.

title: Advanced Data Science with R
description: Equips biology students with vital skills in R programming, statistical analysis, and genomic data analysis. Gain a competitive edge in research and industry by mastering these interdisciplinary techniques essential for modern biological research.

title: Parasitology
description: Parasitism is the most common animal lifestyle. Yet, because parasites are invisible, they are often overlooked. Explore parasite diversity, disease dynamics, and more with an emphasis on the influential roles that parasites play on ecosystem structure and function.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

title: Physiological Plant Ecology
description: An examination of the interactions between plants and their environment. Emphasis on the underlying physiological mechanisms of plant function, adaptations and responses to stress, and the basis of the distribution of plants and plant assemblages across the landscape.
prerequisites_raw: EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 40B or BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

title: Foundations in Neuroimmunology
description: The immune system supports normal brain development as well as controls central nervous system (CNS) infections and augments neurodegenerative and neurological diseases. Assesses how the immune system contributes to both host defense and disease.

title: Chemical Ecology
description: An introduction to the unspoken chemical language of nature. Emphasis on interactions between insects, plants, and microbes including plant defense, pollination, and microbial warfare.
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94 ) and CHEM 51A with a minimum grade of C-

title: Introductory Bioinformatics Lab
description: An introduction to modern methods of analyzing genomic, transcriptomic, and protein structure data. Students design experiments, extract information from a variety of different public databases and synthesize information to gain a deeper understanding of biological systems.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 )

title: Into the Human Brain
description: Explores different methods for studying the human brain in vivo (EEG, MRI, TMS, and others). Discusses ways to measure and manipulate brain activity directly and indirectly and how these different approaches complement each other.

title: Photomedicine
description: Studies the use of optical and engineering-based systems (laser-based) for diagnosis, treating diseases, manipulation of cells and cell function. Physical, optical, and electro-optical principles are explored regarding molecular, cellular, organ, and organism applications.

title: Image Analysis in Biological Research
description: Introduction to scientific image analysis including techniques such as high-speed, time-lapse, thermal imaging, and flow visualization. Students make movies using cameras, edit and analyze images using computers, and do a writing project.
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI E106 or PHRMSCI 120 or BIO SCI E109 ) and ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 )

title: Innate Immunity, Infection, and Pathogenesis
description: Role of the innate immune system in health and disease. Molecular pathways of innate immune recognition, expression, and regulation of immune receptors, signal transduction, pathogen sensors, and detection of microbial ligands. Lecture and discussion of primary research articles.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M122 or BIO SCI M124A or BIO SCI M124B or BIO SCI M143

title: Human Neurodegenerative Diseases
description: Clinical and epidemiological aspects of neurodegenerative diseases causing dementia are reviewed, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, and Frontotemporal Dementia. Seminar format includes student presentation and group discussion.

title: Introduction to Precision Medicine
description: Introduction to the use of genomic techniques for the study of individual genomes and transcriptomes in healthy and diseased samples. Covers GWAS, current sequencing techniques, cancer genomics, and biomarker discovery.

title: Diversity of Fishes
description: A survey of the many dimensions of diversity existing across fishes, the largest group of vertebrate organisms (over 30,000 species). Covers systematics, functional anatomy, development, physiology, biogeography, behavior, and more.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

title: Advances in Regenerative Medicine
description: Introduces the rapidly growing field of regenerative medicine. New developments in stem cell research are discussed. Cellular, molecular, and engineering aspects of stem cell-based organ replacement strategies are examined, with emphasis on specific regenerative therapies.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

title: Environmental Microbiology
description: Focuses on non-pathogenic microbes within all habitats (soils, oceans, associated with animals and plants) and their essential functions for ecosystems. Their applied importance for agriculture, bioremediation, energy and food production are also discussed.

title: Structural Biology
description: Basic principles of magnetic resonance, X-ray crystallography, and CryoEM toward the determination of high-resolution biomolecular structures.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2B or MATH 5B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4

title: Microbiomes
description: Students develop an understanding of microbiomes in the context of both their environment and their impact on host physiology. Discussions on how microbiomes interact with the human body.

title: Cell Biology of Human Disease
description: Builds on prior biology courses about the underlying cell biological mechanisms and recent treatment advances of several model diseases. Emphasizes literature searches, reading primary literature, and student group work.

title: The Physiology of Human Nutrition
description: Examines the biochemical basis of energy metabolism, physiological processes in digestion and uptake, and the biochemical transformation of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins in the human body. The emphasis is on expanding the students' understanding of physiology.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 98 and ( BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120 )

title: Eukaryotic and Human Genetics
description: Structure and function of genes in eukaryotes with emphasis on special problems of genetic studies in humans. Molecular methods of genetic analysis and gene transfer are discussed. Practical applications and ethical and social issues raised by genetic studies are addressed.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

title: Genetics of Complex Traits
description: Many ecologically important traits (e.g., size, age at sexual maturity) and clinical conditions are rooted in the interaction of multiple genetic loci with the environment. Theoretical and practical approaches to dissecting the genetic architecture of complex traits are explored.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

title: Microbial Genetics
description: Basic principles of microbial genetics are presented as lectures for the first half of the course. The second half is devoted to applications of these principles and requires reading review and original research papers and interactions with guest lecturers.

title: Comparative Animal Physiology
description: Maintenance aspects of physiology: water balance; feeding and digestion; metabolism; respiration and circulation.

title: Sex Differences in the Brain
description: Explores the neural bases of sex influences on brain function.

title: Intercellular Signaling and Disease
description: Introduces cell-to-cell communication mechanisms, which are fundamentally essential but still not well understood. From well-established to cutting-edge, researches of intercellular communication and how its malfunction leads to diseases are discussed.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

title: Animal Locomotion
description: The physiology, biomechanics, and neuroscience that determines how animals propel themselves and navigate through the world. Considers the principles that govern the walking, running, flying, and swimming of animals, including exercising humans.

title: Evolution and the Environment Laboratory
description: Explores basic topics in ecology and evolutionary biology and applications to agriculture, conservation, environmental issues, and public health. Format involves lab activities and discussion of scientific journal articles, with focus on learning to evaluate scientific evidence.
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and BIO SCI E106

title: Advanced Cell Biology
description: An in-depth view on general regulatory processes within the cell, with emphasis on research design, techniques, and review of primary literature describing current cell biology research.

title: Human Parasitology
description: Introduction to human animal-parasitic diseases including worms and protozoan infections.

title: Cell Organelles and Membranes
description: Structure, function, and biogenesis of biological membranes and membrane-bound organelles.

title: Genomics, Development, and Medicine
description: Focuses on the applications of genomics and proteomics to problems in genetics, cell, and developmental biology. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the techniques currently used for genomics analysis and how best to apply these tools to solve problems.

title: Animal Coloration and Vision
description: Physiological and behavioral mechanisms of color production and vision including crypsis, mimicry, aposematism, masquerade, sexual dimorphism, and predator-prey interactions through the lens of signals, receivers, and receptors; color and polarization vision in mate choice and visual adaptations to aquatic environments.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI E106 (may be taken concurrently)

title: Behavioral Endocrinology
description: Comparative examination of the major hormone systems that regulate behavior across animals. Emphasizes the reciprocating nature of hormone-behavior interactions and seeks to understand how natural selection drives the evolution of hormone structure and function.

title: Hearing and the Brain
description: An overview of brain mechanisms of hearing, including perception of simple sounds, speech, and music. Begins with sound itself, and looks at processing by the ear, auditory pathways, auditory cortex, and beyond. Also auditory development, learning, and clinical issues.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 160A or BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

title: Conservation Biology
description: Genetic and ecological issues in conservation biology, including effects of human population growth, the value of biodiversity, conservation genetics, demography, metapopulation dynamics, community and ecosystem processes, species invasions, global climate change, and reserve design and management.

title: Biochemistry of Animals in their Environments
description: Interactions between organisms and their environments. Topics include the effects of environmental variables on biochemical functions: membrane stability, protein kinetics, energy metabolism, heat-shock-responses, energetics, gene-expression, and circadian rhythms. These topics are integrated with physiological-ecology in context of global climate change.

title: Developmental Neurobiology
description: The development of the nervous system is discussed with emphasis on the processes that underlie the appearance of complex and highly ordered neural circuits. Topics include neural induction, specification, migration and death; axon growth, and neural circuit formation.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

title: Functional and Structural Evolutionary Genomics
description: Function and organization of genomes analyzed from an evolutionary perspective. Review of some of the most recent experimental approaches in genome analysis and comparative genomics. Relevant software to analyze DNA and expression data is used.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

title: Vascular Biology: Blood Vessels in Health and Disease
description: Every cell in the body is within a half hair’s width of a blood vessel. As such, we cannot understand the body, in health or disease, without understanding the vasculature. Mixes lectures and primary literature reviews.

title: Neuropharmacology
description: Survey of neurotransmitter systems, focusing on how transmitters are made, how they interact with their receptors, and how drugs can influence these processes to alter neural function and behavior.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Genetics and Human History
description: Explores topics in human health/history from an evolutionary perspective, with emphasis on genetics. Topics include the relationship between genetics and human disease as an evolutionary question, and how modern genetic techniques are used to study the history of human populations.

title: Physiology in Extreme Environments
description: An in-depth look at the physiological mechanisms that allow animals, including humans, to be physically active and survive in extreme environments. Physiological responses to high altitude, diving, microgravity, deserts, and extreme cold are examined.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

title: Advanced Cryogenic Electron Microscopy
description: Electron microscopy for biological applications. Practical aspects of cryo-EM, including sample preparation, instrumentation, data collection, and processing methods. Electron crystallography, tomography, and microED. Applications of cryo-EM, current issues and future avenues are discussed along with computational protein design.

title: Neurobiology of Learning and Memory
description: How the brain and behavior change as a result of experience, with an emphasis on identifying the neurochemical processes through which memory is stored and the parts of the brain that are involved.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Biology of Birds Lab
description: A thorough introduction to the biology of birds, covering topics ranging from avian anatomy and physiology to behavior, natural history, ecology, genetics, evolution, systematics, and conservation. Requires field trips to identify local birds and study avian natural history.
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and BIO SCI 94

title: Language and the Brain
description: Research analysis on biological bases of human linguistic capacity. Development, focusing on hemispheric specialization, plasticity; localization of specific linguistic functions in adults, with emphasis on study of aphasias; relation of linguistic capacity to general cognitive capacity, considering research on retardation.
prerequisites_raw: ( COGS 7A or PSCI 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4) or ( COGS 9A or PSCI 11A) and ( COGS 9B or PSCI 11B) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Functional Neuroanatomy
description: How neuroscience uses tools of many disciplines, from imaging to behavior, to develop and test hypotheses about functions of specific parts of the brain. Basic organization of nerve cells/vertebrate nervous system; methods of visualizing nerve cells; neural connections/activity patterns.

title: Brain Disorders and Behavior
description: Examines the localization of human brain functions and the effects of neurological disorders on psychological functions such as perception, motor control, language, memory, and decision-making.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A or PSY 9 or AP Psychology Exam with a minimum score of 4 or ( COGS 9A and COGS 9B ) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Field Biology
description: Conducting group and independent studies in Southern California ecosystems, this course covers the fundamentals of experimental design, statistical analysis, communicating scientific findings (orally, visually, in writing), and other skills necessary for the scientific investigation of biological processes in the field. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and BIO SCI E106 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Evolution
description: An integrative treatment of evolutionary biology that covers evolutionary processes, basic research methods, and the history of life.

title: Applied Human Anatomy
description: Systems approach to analyze the form and function of the human body with an emphasis on applying anatomical concepts to evaluate clinical cases. The laboratory uses human models and a simulated cadaver dissection for structure. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI E109 with a minimum grade of C or PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C or ( BME 120 with a minimum grade of C and BME 121 with a minimum grade of C)

title: Clinical Neuroscience
description: An introduction to the neuroclinical bases of human behavior, including neuropsychological approaches to mental disorders. Also includes case formulations, research articles, therapeutic approaches, and other discussions related to select psychopathology and other neurobehavioral topics.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: PSY 9 or COGS 7A or PSY 21 or COGS 9A or BIO SCI 99

title: Regenerative Neurobiology
description: Explores the field of regenerative neurobiology. Both basic stem cell discoveries and their potential clinical application to brain disorders examined. Opportunities, challenges, and implications of this research also discussed.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Human Neuropsychology
description: A survey of human brain disorders using a clinical case study approach to illustrate fundamental issues in studying brain and behavior. Topics include sensory deficits, attentional neglect, amnesia, cortical organization, clinical psychopathology, and more.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or COGS 9A

title: Principles of Neural Computation
description: Introduction to the theoretical principles and biological mechanisms underlying how brains acquire, assimilate, store, and retrieve information, and how they compute adaptive responses to external inputs.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Cerebral Cortex: Structure, Function, and Plasticity
description: The cerebral cortex is highly developed in mammals and is responsible for higher perceptual and cognitive functions. Explores some amazing aspects of cortical structure, function, and plasticity emphasizing primary literature.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Limnology and Freshwater Biology
description: Biology of freshwater environments: lakes, ponds, rivers, their biota, and the factors which influence distribution of organisms.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

title: Field Freshwater Ecology
description: Analytical techniques for common water-quality variables of lakes, streams, and rivers. Benthic fauna, vertebrates and invertebrates, algae, and aquatic plants. Emphasis on field methods with an experimental approach; laboratory exercises. Field trips to marshes, vernal pools, rivers, and streams. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 ) and BIO SCI E179

title: Biotechnological Applications of Energy and Environmental Research
description: Covers microbiological and biochemical background related to current biotechnological applications, case studies of biotech-companies, and basic information related to patents and start-up companies. Topics include biofuel, bioremediation, agricultural, and environmental applications.

title: Vision
description: Visual perception and the anatomy and physiology of the visual system. Topics include the retina and the visual pathway; visual sensitivity; color vision; spatial vision; motion perception; and the development of the visual system.

title: Exercise Physiology
description: Focus upon critical topics in the area of exercise biology using the comparative physiological approach. Specifically examine the physiological factors that limit the capacity of an organism to sustain high levels of aerobic metabolism.

title: Ecology and Diversity of Insects
description: Insects—representing two-thirds of all species—play fundamental roles in human health, agriculture, and natural ecosystems. Topics include insect morphology, development, physiology, taxonomy, ecology, and insects in human affairs. Lecture includes interactive demonstrations and an optional weekend trip. Materials Fee

title: Population and Community Ecology Lab
description: Covers processes specific to groups of the same species (populations) and multiple species (communities). Includes growth, regulation, dynamics, and persistence of populations and community interactions, development, diversity, and macroecology. Lab activities focus on application of population prediction and biodiversity assessment.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI E106 and ( BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108 )

title: Exercise as Medicine
description: Explores the link between regular physical activity and health, focusing on mechanistic insights into how regular exercise improves overall health and alters disease trajectories of cancer, type-II diabetes, depression, and other chronic illnesses.

title: Environmental Ethics
description: History of evolution of environmental ethics in America. Management problems in national parks, wilderness areas, wild and scenic rivers, national forests. Contemporary and historical aspects/contributors to the field. Mitigation, endangered species, habitat restoration, biodiversity, and environmental activism. Field trips required.

title: Transfer Student Seminar
description: Weekly meetings consisting of presentations by faculty, professional staff, and New Student Peer Academic Advisors provide information about the School of Biological Sciences, campus resources, and special programs/opportunities.

title: Topics in Developmental and Cell Biology
description: Studies in selected areas of developmental and cell biology.

title: Topics in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
description: Studies in selected areas of ecology and evolutionary biology.

title: Topics in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
description: Studies in selected areas of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry.

title: Topics in Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Studies in selected areas of neurobiology and behavior.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability I
description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations. Prepare bibliography.

title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability II
description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations. Prepare research proposal.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 191A or SOCECOL 186A or EARTHSS 190A

title: Writing/Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability III
description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum also is required. Seminar utilized to analyze Forum presentations and to prepare senior research paper. Prepare/write research paper under direction of faculty member.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B . BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Topics in Biological Sciences Tutoring
description: Tutoring programs with biological sciences student peers.

title: Biological Sciences Learning Assistant Mentoring
description: Oversight of trained learning assistants by the course instructor, including training in the discipline and responsibilities associated with supporting active group work. Instructor mentors LAs in how assisting small groups supports their career goals.

title: Center for Environmental Biology Internship
description: Focuses on the theory and practice of ecological research and education and outreach, especially related to the management of natural resources.

title: Campus as a Living Lab I
description: Students study sustainability concepts and theories and how they apply to our most pressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. Concurrently, they work on hands-on projects to improve the sustainability of campus operations and systems.

title: Campus as a Living Lab II
description: Students study sustainability concepts and theories and how they apply to our most pressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. Concurrently, they work on hands-on projects to improve the sustainability of campus operations and systems.

title: Campus as a Living Lab III
description: Students study sustainability concepts and theories and how they apply to our most pressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. Concurrently, they work on hands-on projects to improve the sustainability of campus operations and systems.

title: Honors Topics in Biological Sciences
description: Varied course topics in Biological Sciences designed for students in Honors in Biological Sciences.

title: Special Study in Biological Sciences
description: Individualized instruction dealing with conceptual or theoretical problems in the biological sciences, rather than technical problems.

title: Independent Study in Biological Sciences Research
description: Individual experimental laboratory or field research under a professor's direction. Required for participation in the Excellence in Research Program.

title: Research Writing
description: Development of research skills such as learning how to plan and conduct research experiments, read and analyze scientific journal articles, and practice presenting the data experiments and journal articles with an emphasis on scientific writing.

title: Political Economy: Methods and Critique
description: Introduction to canonical texts in Marxism coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken after CLT&THY 200B .

title: Libidinal Economy: Methods and Critique
description: Introduction to canonical texts in psychoanalysis coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken before CLT&THY 200A .

title: Theory from Below
description: Introduction to systems of thought understudied or undervalued in academic canons; for instance, systems constituted in communities' practices or theories that do not seek permanence or generality.

title: Independent Study
description: Limited to students who have not yet received the M.A. degree.

title: Topics in Culture and Theory
description: Seminars on various topics in Culture and Theory.

title: Directed Reading
description: Directed readings on a specific topic agreed upon by students and their instructors. Limited to students who have completed their M.A. degree and are preparing for their qualifying exam.

title: Introduction to Theatre
description: An interactive introduction to the world of theatre that serves to develop an appreciation of theatrical arts, to establish an awareness of landmarks within the performance history, and to create an understanding of the collaborative roles and departments that exist.

title: The Rock and Roll Spectacle Show
description: A thorough overview to the development and cultural significance of the Rock 'n' Roll Spectacle show. Focus on historical and recent developments of the spectacle show, trends in the aesthetics of the field, and various sub-genres.

title: Music Theatre Today
description: An interactive and thorough overview of 21st century music theatre. Develops an appreciation and awareness of the contemporary musical on stage today, current trends in the development of new music theatre work, and the art form’s global expansion.

title: Food, Film, Power
description: Food is the ambassador of cultures. The journey of food maps the history of human civilization. Examines feature films, documentaries, shorts, and writings on food, and analyzes the geopolitics, economics, migration, culture, performativity, and power of food.

title: Performing Rock 'N' Roll
description: Explores major movements in the history of rock 'n' roll in terms of performance, not virtuosity necessarily of the performers as musicians, rather as performances of aesthetics in modes of embodied ideology, iconoclastic spectacle, mixed media fashion, and subcultural formation.

title: Performance Now
description: Exposes students to what is most current in the world of performance and theatre. Begins with a series of lectures on the idea of performance, and the various theories that frame it.

title: Performing Culture
description: Culture, aesthetics, and ideology (combined in the concept "subculture") work to fashion social identities. Using theories and methodologies of performance studies, with an emphasis on American culture, explores why and how culture is reinforced through performance.

title: Culture in Performance
description: A three-quarter foundation series exploring the rich depth of theatre, drama, and other genres of performance across a wide variety of worldwide forms, for performer and audience.

title: Culture in Performance
description: A three-quarter foundation series exploring the rich depth of theatre, drama, and other genres of performance across a wide variety of worldwide forms, for performer and audience.

title: Culture in Performance
description: A three-quarter foundation series exploring the rich depth of theatre, drama, and other genres of performance across a wide variety of worldwide forms, for performer and audience.

title: Applied Improvisation
description: An introduction to Applied Improvisation (AI), the improvisational mindset, the current trends and historic uses of AI, and concepts and techniques from improvised theatre that can help individuals achieve their goals beyond creating comedy.

title: Acting
description: Focuses on Stanislavski-based terminology and technique through theatre exercises and improvisation. The first part of a one-year series in basic acting technique and discipline.

title: Acting
description: Focuses on scene work and character development. The second part of a one-year series in basic acting technique and discipline.

title: Acting
description: Focuses on monologues, auditions, callbacks, and the profession of acting. The third part of a one-year series in basic acting technique and discipline.

title: Movement for Actors
description: Fundamentals of stretch, strength, and alignment; exploring spatial awareness and physical control through mime isolations, techniques, and related improvisation.

title: Speech for the Theatre
description: An introductory course in voice and speech for actors, combining the body-based approach to voice developed by Fitzmaurice, and speech work of Knight and Thompson. Designed for the needs of actors and is not a public speaking course.

title: Development of Drama
description: The development of Western Drama, concentrating on the drama’s intellectual, social, and artistic foundations. About 10 plays and supplementary critical material are read each quarter. Greek Drama through Shakespeare.

title: Development of Drama
description: The development of Western Drama, concentrating on the drama’s intellectual, social, and artistic foundations. About 10 plays and supplementary critical material are read each quarter. Restoration Drama through Ibsen.

title: Development of Drama
description: The development of Western Drama, concentrating on the drama’s intellectual, social, and artistic foundations. About 10 plays and supplementary material are read each quarter. Contemporary Drama. Post Naturalistic theatre.

title: Introduction to Costume Design
description: Introduction to the process and procedures employed by the costume designer for the theatre. The elements of design are discussed in the context of character development, historical period, and style. Exercises extend to drawing, rendering, and investigation of human proportions.

title: Introduction to Scenic Design
description: Introduction to the principles and practice of scenic design. Weekly problems include research into various periods and styles of production with an emphasis on the conceptual idea. Perspective drawing, rendering, and model building are covered in studio exercises and assignments.

title: Introduction to Lighting Design
description: Introduction to the principles, theories, and equipment employed by the lighting designer for the stage. Areas of investigation include history, technology, and script analysis. Detailed studio attention is given to the theory and practice of design.

title: Introduction to Sound Design
description: Principles, theories, equipment use, and terminology employed by the sound designer for the stage. Areas of study include history, technology, and script analysis. Focuses on the theory and practice of design.

title: Introduction to Stage Management
description: A basic study of theatrical, dance, and opera stage management practices, forms, and methods, from first script reading to closing night. Opportunity to observe professionals at work in regional and touring situations as available.

title: Introduction to Lighting and Sound Design
description: Provides a thorough overview to the art and craft of theatrical lighting and sound design. Class time is roughly split between the two fields, and roughly split between technology and creativity.

title: Introduction to Costume Design and Stage Management
description: Provides a thorough overview to the art and craft of theatrical costume design and stage management. Class time is roughly split between the two fields, and roughly split between technology and creativity.

title: Introduction to Scenic and Video Design
description: Provides a thorough overview to the art and craft of theatrical scenic and projection design. Class time is roughly split between the two fields, and roughly split between technology and creativity.

title: Topics in Advanced Stage Management
description: Nurtures a greater appreciation for the stage manager and his or her process, and supports students who are interested in pursuing a career in professional stage management.

title: Music Theatre Workshop I
description: Basic vocal technique and characterization of musical theatre repertoire explored.

title: Directing I
description: Introduction to comprehensive directing process from pre-production to opening. Focus on fundamental skills: analysis, staging, action, actor coaching, and elements of design. Skills applied to scripted theatrical material. Develop a language for commenting on theatrical production. Attending and critiquing productions.

title: Laboratory for Creative Collaboration
description: Allows students to do immediate, hands-on creative work, while preparing them for a wide range of careers in arts and in arts-adjacent fields as well as in a wide variety of industries.

title: University Theatre
description: Rehearsal and performance in a faculty-directed production.

title: Theatre Production: Costume
description: The production courses are offered to give students the opportunity to participate in departmental productions. Students engage in the production and construction of designed work as well as its applied execution during performance.

title: Theatre Production: Scenic
description: The production courses are offered to give students the opportunity to participate in departmental productions. Students engage in the production and construction of designed work as well as its applied execution during performance.

title: Theatre Production: Stage Management

title: Theatre Production: Audio
description: The production courses are offered to give students the opportunity to participate in departmental productions. Students engage in the production and construction of designed work as well as its applied execution during performance.

title: Theatre Production: Theatre Management
description: The production courses are offered to give students the opportunity to participate in departmental productions. Students engage in the production and construction of designed work as well as its applied execution during performance.

title: Topics in Dramatic Literature
description: Courses include Medieval and Tudor Drama, Elizabethan and Jacobean Drama, Shakespeare, Restoration and 18th Century Drama, Modern British Drama, Modern American Drama, Tragedy, and Comedy.

title: Lectures in Dramatic Literature
description: Courses include Medieval and Tudor Drama, Elizabethan and Jacobean Drama, Shakespeare, Restoration and Eighteenth-Century Drama, Modern British Drama, Modern American Drama, Tragedy, and Comedy.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Theory and Criticism
description: Discussion of recent major trends and ideas in critical theory, concentrating on in-depth readings and lectures in particular facets of theory and criticism: Derrida, Butler, Lacan, Deleuze, and others.

title: Special Topics in Theory and Criticism
description: Discussion of recent major trends and ideas in critical theory, concentrating on in-depth readings and lectures in particular facets of theory and criticism: Derrida, Butler, Lacan, Deleuze, and others.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Classical Dramas
description: Designed to introduce students to various classical traditions-early Greek and Roman theatres, to be sure, but also, by way of comparison, the classical traditions of non-European cultures.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 40A or DRAMA 40B or DRAMA 40C . Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Early Modern and Neoclassical Theatre
description: Investigates aspects of European theatre and culture in the sixteenth, seventeenth, and eighteenth centuries; individual courses may focus on specific topics within this broad expanse.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Nineteenth-Century Dramas
description: Looks at the various trends and conventions of theatres in the nineteenth century, both Euro-American and beyond, paying special attention to the culture and political milieu within which these various traditions appeared.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 40A and DRAMA 40B and DRAMA 40C . Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Nineteenth-Century Dramas
description: Looks at the various trends and conventions of theatres in the nineteenth century, both Euro-American and beyond, paying special attention to the culture and political milieu within which these various traditions appeared.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 40A and DRAMA 40B and DRAMA 40C . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Modern and Contemporary Drama
description: An investigation into the many forms and permutations of modern (1880-1945), and contemporary (since 1945) drama, paying special attention to the historical and philosophical interpretations of text and performance.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 40A and DRAMA 40B and DRAMA 40C . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Modern and Contemporary Drama
description: An investigation into the many forms and permutations of modern (1880-1945), and contemporary (since 1945) drama, paying special attention to the historical and philosophical interpretations of text and performance.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 40A and DRAMA 40B and DRAMA 40C . Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Introduction to Asian Theatre
description: An introduction to some of the major traditional theatrical forms and dramatic texts from India, China, and Japan. Other than dramatic texts (in English translation), attention is also paid to theory, history, and performance styles of traditional Asian theatre.

title: Asian American Theatre
description: An introduction to the history and development of Asian American theatre and drama. Besides play analysis, special attention is also paid to the history and politics of Asian American identity and experience, as well as to aspects of theatrical performance.

title: Multicultural Theatres
description: A study of the history, culture, aesthetics, and literature of various traditional performing arts and their connections to the contemporary multicultural society.

title: African American Film and Drama
description: A critical investigation of films and plays written by African Americans, with emphasis on dramaturgical and cinematic strategies, individual and collective representation, and the legacy of African American political struggle.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: African American Film and Drama
description: A critical investigation of films and plays written by African Americans, with emphasis on dramaturgical and cinematic strategies, individual and collective representation, and the legacy of African American political struggle.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Advanced Topics in Performance
description: Addresses particular issues in theatre and performance that typically lie outside of regular course offerings. May address such issues as the theatre of the Avant Garde, performing gender, transversality and performance, body art, installation and performance art, among other topics.

title: Advanced Topics in Performance
description: Addresses particular issues in theatre and performance that typically lie outside of regular course offerings. May address such issues as the theatre of the Avant Garde, performing gender, transversality and performance, body art, installation and performance art, among other topics.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Intermediate Acting
description: Rehearsal and presentation of scenes from contemporary material. Focus on connection with scene partner, playing actions, and text analysis. Introduction to the credibility and theatricality of characterization and style.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 30A and DRAMA 30B and DRAMA 30C with an average grade of B or better. For transfer students: one year of beginning acting with an average grade of B or better

title: Topics in Writing for Performance
description: Completion of a short play or its equivalent; discussion of student writing and of relevant literary texts.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Studio for Advanced Movement for Actors
description: Studio course in conditioning and partnering techniques to the practice of contact improvisation. Contact improvisation is explored and applied in scene study.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 34 with a minimum grade of B

title: Master Classes in Acting
description: Advanced acting in specialized areas including acting for the camera: situation comedy; commercials; auditioning and industry preparation; Shakespeare; Molière; Chekov; improvisation; advanced movement and voice and speech for the actor; self-starting; stage combat; repertory acting, singing; comedy; clowning; and masks.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 130 with a minimum grade of B

title: Music Theatre Acting
description: An acting class exclusive to the students in the B.F.A. in Music Theatre program.

title: Music Theatre Workshop II
description: A workshop in audition technique and song interpretation.

title: Music Theatre Workshop III
description: Scene study and song repertoire examined by era for the advanced Music Theatre student. 1800s-1940.

title: Music Theatre Workshop III
description: Scene study and song repertoire examined by era for the advanced Music Theatre student. 1940s-1970s.

title: Music Theatre Workshop III
description: Scene study and song repertoire examined by era for the advanced Music Theatre student. 1970's-present.

title: Music Theatre Workshop IV
description: A performance class concentrating on role building. Work culminates with in-class performances of abbreviated versions of musicals.
prerequisites_raw: For B.F.A. students: DRAMA 143A , DRAMA 143B , DRAMA 143C , and audition. For Drama graduate students: audition required

title: Music Theatre Singing
description: Private weekly voice lessons for the advanced Music Theatre student.

title: NYSP-Preparation
description: Class preparation for the New York Satellite Program (NYSP) - an immersion experience in New York City for the musical theatre performer.
prerequisites_raw: Admission is by audition and the following prerequisites: DRAMA 30C and two quarters of DRAMA 148A , DRAMA 148B , or DRAMA 148C (if the 148 prerequisite is not complete at the time of auditions, student must enroll during the fall and winter quarters in the same year as the trip to New York); senior Drama majors must have successfully completed DRAMA 40C and DRAMA 120C; non-Drama majors must have sophomore standing or higher and must carefully plan their course schedule as many spring quarter classes cannot be taken while part of the NYSP

title: History of American Musical Theatre
description: A survey of the influential artists who produce, write, direct, and perform on America's musical stages. Surveys 1800s-1960s.

title: History of American Musical Theatre
description: A survey of the influential artists who produce, write, direct, and perform on America's musical stages. Surveys 1970s-present.

title: Music Proficiency for Actors
description: A musicianship class introducing basic musical terminology, theory, and sight singing skills.

title: Costume Production Techniques
description: Studio instruction in pattern making, draping, millinery, and construction techniques.

title: Lighting Composition
description: Provides an opportunity for students to pursue stage lighting composition in a studio atmosphere. Laboratory practice includes weekly exercises in style and genre. Emphasis is placed on the realization of conceptual ideas.

title: Topics in Theatre Design
description: Examines the various functions of scenery and costume: locale, historical period, mood, and atmosphere, with special assignments in each area. Discussion of problems in scenic metaphors and visualization, emphasizing techniques of planning and presentation (e.g., floor plans, models, and rendering).

title: Proseminar in Theatre Design
description: Topics in theatre design.

title: History of Costume
description: A study of the development of dress and the influence of cultural factors on clothing from the time of Egyptians to Early Baroque.

title: History of Costume
description: A study of the development of dress and the influence of cultural factors on clothing from late Baroque to World War I.

title: Script and Score
description: A form and analysis seminar discussing the libretto and score of landmark musicals.
prerequisites_raw: Two courses from DRAMA 148A or DRAMA 148B or DRAMA 148C

title: Song Repertoire
description: A song coaching class culminating in a song recital or showcase. Each quarter will feature a different composer, lyricist, or musical style.

title: Contemporary Dramatic Criticism and Theory
description: Reading and analysis of theories and critical approaches to contemporary theatre: Brecht, Artaud, and others who have contributed to the form and idea of the modern theatre. Writing of assigned exercises in dramatic criticism.

title: Dance Technique, Level I
description: Advanced beginner and intermediate dance training including musical theatre, ballet, jazz and contemporary modern techniques and repertoire. Body conditioning is also a major component of the course.

title: Dance Technique, Level I
description: Advanced beginner and intermediate dance training including musical theatre, ballet, jazz and contemporary modern techniques and repertoire. Body conditioning is also a major component of the course.
prerequisites_raw: ( DRAMA 65 or DRAMA 142 ) and DRAMA 182A . Audition required

title: Dance Technique, Level II
description: Intermediate and advanced dance training including musical theatre, ballet, jazz and contemporary modern techniques and repertoire. Body conditioning is also a major component of the course.

title: Dance Technique, Level II
description: Intermediate and advanced dance training including musical theatre, ballet, jazz and contemporary modern techniques and repertoire. Body conditioning is also a major component of the course.
prerequisites_raw: ( DRAMA 65 or DRAMA 142 ) and DRAMA 183A . Audition required

title: Topics in Directing II
description: The principles of stage directing, covering the director's functions in the areas of interpretation, composition, coaching, and styling a theatrical production. Directing exercises and projects; the final project is the preparation of a hypothetical proposal for a play production.
prerequisites_raw: DRAMA 30A and DRAMA 30B and DRAMA 40A and DRAMA 40B and DRAMA 40C and DRAMA 80

title: Advanced Directing
description: A seminar in directorial organization and research. Student prepares a textual and dramaturgical analysis, a production timetable, and a hypothetical production book of an assigned play.

title: NYSP-Acting
description: New York Satellite Program acting classes taught by guest faculty in New York.

title: NYSP - Dance
description: New York Satellite Program dance classes in ballet, tap, jazz, and musical theatre styles taught by guest faculty in New York.

title: NYSP - Singing
description: New York Satellite Program private and group lessons in musical theatre singing taught by guest faculty in New York.

title: NYSP - Performance
description: New York Satellite Program rehearsals and public, staged readings of original musicals in New York.

title: NYSP-UCI Residency
description: New York Satellite Program follow-up classes and performances back on Irvine campus upon the return from New York.

title: Director Class Project
description: For students who are involved in the Director Class Projects at UCI as actors, directors, designers, stage managers and their assistants. M.F.A. Directors and the Head of Directing (HoD) supervise the projects.

title: Project in Theatre
description: Independent theatre projects with Drama faculty.

title: Graduate Studio: Acting
description: Work in graduate studio taken in tandem with graduate studios in stage voice ( DRAMA 201 ), stage speech ( DRAMA 202 ), and stage movement ( DRAMA 203 ).

title: Graduate Studio: Voice
description: Graduate studio in vocal production for actors.

title: Graduate Studio: Speech
description: Graduate studio in speech for actors.

title: Graduate Studio: Movement
description: Work in graduate studio: stage movement taken in tandem with nine graduate studios in acting ( DRAMA 200 ), voice ( DRAMA 201 ), speech ( DRAMA 202 ), and voice/movement dynamics ( DRAMA 206 ).

title: Graduate Studio: Voice/Movement Dynamics
description: Daily conditioning exercises.

title: Graduate Master Class
description: Various topics such as Shakespeare, comedy, Molière, improvisation, Kabuki, television acting.

title: Seminar in Dramatic Literature
description: Topics in Dramatic Literature.

title: Seminar on Theatre Pedagogy
description: A seminar on the major teaching systems in the dramatic arts with particular attention to professional arts training. Required prior to applying for Teaching Assistantships in studio areas.

title: Graduate Projects
description: Various projects depending on student’s concentration (acting, design, musical theatre, directing).

title: Singing Pedagogy
description: Learning how to teach voice lessons and coach musical theatre singing. Experiences include both private voice lessons and observing the lessons given to the B.F.A./Music Theatre students.

title: Conducting
description: Private conducting instruction to develop freedom of movement/expression, baton technique, ear training, and tempo memory for both rehearsal and performance situations in musical theatre.

title: Dramaturgy: Theory and Methods
description: Examines the practice, place, and theory of dramaturgy. Explores plays in terms of how they work: dramatic form and structure, historical context, and more. Study includes dramaturgy as a theatrical practice.
